clues: A dry valley on the west bank of a great river, opposite the ancient city of Thebes, where the rulers of a kingdom were buried in rock-cut tombs.
In November 1922 an archaeologist opened the tomb of a young pharaoh here, one of the most famous finds in archaeology.

reveal.placeName: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt
reveal.explanation: The Valley of the Kings is a wadi on the west bank of the Nile, opposite Thebes, the modern-day Luxor. Its tombs were cut for the pharaohs of Egypt's New Kingdom; Howard Carter discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62) there in November 1922.

sources.excerpt: The Valley of the Kings (25.74083°N 32.60222°E) is a wadi sitting on the west bank of the Nile, opposite Thebes (modern-day Luxor). Howard Carter discovered the actual tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62) in November 1922.
